title: Economic activity, and financial and commodity markets’ shocks: an analysis of implied volatility indexes
summary: The paper examines short- and long-run asymmetric interactions and causality between real economic activity and volatility shocks in stock, energy and gold markets. The relationships are asymmetric at both horizons.
keyFindings: Positive and negative energy-market shocks both raise stock-market volatility in the long run.
The energy market is the main net transmitter of shocks; gold is a net receiver.
There is feedback between economic activity and the volatility indexes, except for gold, which causes economic activity in one direction only.
methods: Nonlinear ARDL cointegration and Granger causality tests, with Diebold–Yilmaz spillover indexes on partial-sum decompositions.
